To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tail artery of the young (2- and 6-month-old) spontaneously hypertenisve rat (SHR) exhibits a distinct enhancement of active sodium extrusion and potassium uptake compared with age-mated Wistar-Kyto controls, while the tail artery of rats with hypertension induced by renal constriction does not.

1) active Na+ extrusion is enhanced in the tail artery of young spontaneously hypertensive rats, 2) this enhancement is not observed in the renal artery of rats with renal artery hypertension, and 3) cell potassium is elevated and cell sodium is constrained in the tail artery in young spontaneously hypertensive rat, but not in rats with renal artery hypeension.
the active extrusion of sodium is enhanced in the tail artery of the spontaneously hypertensive rat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the sympathetic nervous system in hypertension.
the mechanism of hypertension and the role of Na, K+ ATPase in the development of hypertension.
the mechanisms by which the blood vessels of the spontaneously hypertensive rats differ from the vessels of normotensive Wistar-Kyotos.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SHR tail artery exhibits a distinct and early increase in the capacity for active Na+ extrusion, which is not associated with increased cell sodium or potassium, but which may be related to an increased permeability of the cell membrane.
the SHR exhibits an enhanced capacity for active Na extrusion and passive Na permeability.
the SHR tail artery has a higher cell potassium content and a lower cell sodium content than does the tail artery of the age-matched WKY control rat at 2, 4, 6, 12, and 26 weeks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the young, but not the adult SHR, the enhanced sodium transport is associated with a significant increase in cell potassium.
young SHR have an increased capacity for active Na+ extrusion, which may be due to a higher number of active sites for the Na+ pump.
young, normotensive SHR are hyperkinetic in their vascular smooth muscle, and this may be the cause rather than the effect of hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the increased cell potassium and the increased cell permeability to sodium and potassium are not due to the increased cell potassium.
young SHR have enhanced active sodium transport and elevated cell potassium.
young SHR are characterized by enhanced active Na transport and elevated cell K.
